findings.title: Phase output bypasses the active progress row's sole-writer contract
findings.detail: crates/blit-core/src/transfer_session/phase_probe.rs:243 writes and flushes raw stderr synchronously from run_local_session, while crates/blit-cli/src/transfers/local.rs:571 declares the live progress writer the sole owner of transfer-time stderr. Interactive CLI runs enable that row automatically, and the phase report is emitted before the caller clears it, so progress control writes can interleave with or scroll away the sole JSON artifact; the blocking write also runs on the async worker. Route the report through the row-aware output path or defer it until the row is closed.

findings.title: Failed sessions emit reports with silently incomplete phase timings
findings.detail: crates/blit-core/src/transfer_session/local.rs:770 deliberately emits before checking the session faults, but crates/blit-core/src/transfer_session/mod.rs:4966 applies ? before closing the Compare span and line 4993 applies ? before recording Plan; source enumeration has the same record-after-success shape. A scan, comparison, or plan that fails after substantial work therefore emits that phase as zero or incomplete with no failure/partial marker, contradicting the stated purpose of timing slow failed runs and potentially selecting the wrong phase.
